workItems.note: One page holding both resource kinds, confirmed by the user.

'Not an error and not retryable by us' - the customer must add the DNS record.
suspend from active, resume from suspended, retry_provision from failed, mark_failed from provisioning|active.
my-expert-sites and my-agent-workspace both return arrays scoped to the viewer.

unknowns: Whether one user can hold more than one agent workspace. my-agent-workspace is named singular but returns [AgentWorkspaceEntity]; the contract was believed over the name.
What the DNS instruction surface shows. my-expert-site-deployment exists but its fields were not read in this run.
Whether mark_failed should be reachable from this page. Its enum comment calls it an interim owner-triggered producer of failed because no provisioning watcher exists yet.
Where 'dashboard expert' belongs. page-dashboard for apps/app is already owned by case-d1 and apps/expert has no pages; deliberately not planned here.

businessCapabilities.capability: counts of resources grouped by status

directions.thesis: The page opens with work that needs a person; running resources sit below. Awaiting-DNS and Failed share one queue but carry two different sentences: one names the customer's job, one names our failure.
tradeoffs: A resource changes position when its status changes, so the list does not stay still.

exactProposals.api: props: { name, detail, reason, status }, on: { act }

directions.thesis: Expert sites and agent workspaces are two lifecycles, so they sit on two labelled shelves. Status is a fact on the row, not the page's headline.
tradeoffs: Awaiting-DNS is buried in a shelf; a user with several sites must hunt for the one thing blocking a launch.

exactProposals.api: props: { name, detail, status }, on: { act }

directions.thesis: Both resource kinds normalize onto one row shape (name, kind, status, action) in a single list, with a status counter strip above and a kind filter between them.
tradeoffs: Normalizing erases real differences: suspend/resume exists only for workspaces, awaiting-DNS only for sites. A shared row can imply actions that do not exist for that kind.
The counter strip needs a backend enabler; without it the counts are computed client-side and become wrong the moment the list paginates.
